s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent painful skin lesions with ulceration and systemic symptoms
salient_findings: Painful pimple-like bumps on bilateral lower legs
Ulcers with central eschars and dusky gray borders
key_facts: Patient is a young black woman
Presented with chills and bilateral lower extremity swelling
Recent course of trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole for methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus
Medical history includes treatment with methimazole and atenolol
Laboratory tests show elevated C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate
Normal C3 and C4 complement levels
ANA titer 1:80
P-ANCA titer 1:20
Anti-myeloperoxidase titer 141 U
Anti-SSA/Ro antibodies level 120 U
Punch biopsy showed mid- and deep dermal lymphohistiocytic infiltrate with neutrophils and focal abscess
Second biopsy showed intraepidermal and dermal perivascular neutrophilic infiltrate with necrosis of vessel walls

shortlist.label: Microscopic polyangiitis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated anti-myeloperoxidase titer and perivascular neutrophilic infiltrate

shortlist.label: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Necrosis of vessel walls and perivascular neutrophilic infiltrate

shortlist.label: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
shortlist.why_kept: Systemic symptoms and elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate

shortlist.label: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Skin lesions with ulceration and systemic symptoms

shortlist.label: Methimazole-induced vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Recent treatment with methimazole and vasculitic skin lesions

raw.rationale: The patient's medical history includes treatment with methimazole, and the laboratory tests and biopsy results are consistent with vasculitis, which can be induced by methimazole

rejected.label: Microscopic polyangiitis
rejected.why: While the patient has elevated anti-myeloperoxidase titer, the clinical presentation and biopsy results are more consistent with a drug-induced vasculitis

rejected.label: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis
rejected.why: This is a possible diagnosis, but the patient's history of methimazole use makes methimazole-induced vasculitis a more likely cause

rejected.label: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
rejected.why: The patient's biopsy results do not show granulomas, which are characteristic of this disease

rejected.label: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome
rejected.why: This is a genetic disorder that is not consistent with the patient's acute presentation of vasculitis
